newsitem.title: USA: Congress to probe charges of improper IRS audits.
newsitem.headline: Congress to probe charges of improper IRS audits.

text.p: Top lawmakers on Monday announced they were launching an investigation into charges that the Internal Revenue Service had carried out politically motivated audits of conservative, tax-exempt organisations.

The chairmen and ranking Democrats on the House Ways and Means and Senate Finance Committees asked staff to look into reports the IRS had singled out the Heritage Foundation, National Rifle Association and other right-leaning groups.

"We are troubled by recent reports alleging politically motivated treatment of certain tax-exempt organisations and individuals," the bipartisan group said in a letter to Congress' nonpartisan Joint Committee on Taxation.
"These allegations are very serious and should be carefully reviewed as expeditiously as possible," it said.

The letter was signed by Texas Republican Representative Bill Archer, New York Democratic Representative Charles Rangel, Delaware Republican Sen. William Roth and New York Democratic Sen. Daniel Patrick Moynihan.
IRS Commissioner Margaret Milner Richardson said she was "delighted" by the lawmakers' decision to give her agency a chance to clear the air. She had suggested a similar review in February.
"I stated then and I continue to believe that these reports are inaccurate and misleading and could erode the public confidence in the integrity of our ... system," she said in a statement.

Because audits are confidential, the IRS cannot respond publicly to what the commissioner termed "false allegations, innuendos and suggestions" of impropriety without permission from the affected entity.

Conservative groups have made the alleged targeting a cause celebre, complaining the audits are part of a pattern of harassment. Among organisations being audited are groups that have been connected to House Speaker Newt Gingrich.
The audits have come to light because the affected organisations disclosed them. Liberal groups have not stepped forward with similar information.

"It is possible that it is sheer coincidence that every group on the Clinton enemies list is being audited ... but it's also possible it's not," Grover Norquist, president of Americans for Tax Reform, said.
"We need to know that and have the assurance that it isn't being politicized," he said.
Organisations set up under section 501(c)(3) of the tax code are tax-exempt and supporters can deduct donations. Such organisations are limited regarding allowable lobbying.
In addition, 501(c)(4) groups are tax exempt, but such groups are not typically organised as charities and individuals do not receive tax deductions for contributions.

Because audits are confidential, regular committees cannot delve into the charges at a public hearing. Under federal law, the IRS can disclose limited tax information to the Joint Committee on Taxation.

The lawmakers said they expected the joint committee to issue a report. They asked the panel to investigate whether the audits had been politically motivated, including whether they were related to any lobbying activities.
